question.problem: At a particular underwater location, earthquakes occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of once every $2.5$ months. Determine the probability that the next quake will not happen for at least $6$ months. Round your answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since the earthquakes occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next earthquake using an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the amount of time until the next earthquake. Since there is an earthquake every $2.5$ months on average, the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{2.5}=2/5$ earthquakes per month.

The number of earthquakes can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =2/5,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{5}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{e}^{-2x/5}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the next earthquake will not occur for at least $6$ months is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & ={\int }_{6}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{6}^{\infty }\frac{2}{5}{e}^{-2x/5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-{e}^{-2x/5}|}_{6}^{\infty } \\  & =-{e}^{-\infty }+{e}^{-12/5} \\  & =0+{e}^{-12/5} \\  & ={e}^{-12/5} \\  & ≈0.0907.\end{aligned}
$$
